commitMessage: DEV-20: Build bounded context artifact loader
objective: Create a deterministic, read-only context artifact loader that safely loads bounded textual content for DEV-19 relevant repository entries while enforcing repository boundaries, protected-path restrictions, file-size limits, per-artifact limits, total context limits, binary-file rejection, truncation metadata, and stable ordering for downstream reasoning systems.
architecturalContext: River Development Agent roadmap Generation II
acceptanceCriteria: The loader accepts deterministic relevant repository entries produced by the DEV-19 Context Engine.
Only repository-relative file entries are eligible for content loading.
Directories are not loaded as textual artifacts.
Protected paths and protected classifications are never read as context artifacts.
Paths that resolve outside the repository boundary are rejected.
Binary or non-text files are rejected or represented without exposing binary content.
Each loaded artifact records its repository-relative path, classification, selection reason, original byte size, loaded byte count, truncation state, and textual content.
Per-artifact content is bounded by a deterministic maximum size.
The complete loaded context is bounded by a deterministic total byte budget.
Artifacts are processed in stable deterministic order.
When the total context budget is exhausted, later artifacts are omitted deterministically and the result records omission counts.
UTF-8 text files are loaded without introducing byte-order-mark content into the resulting context.
Missing files and unreadable files produce deterministic safe failures rather than silent corruption.
DEV-19 development context can include the loaded artifact bundle without changing repository state.
The context command reports loaded artifact counts, loaded bytes, truncation counts, omission counts, and artifact paths.
The loader performs read-only repository access and never modifies application files.
Focused tests, existing DEV-19 regressions, River Dev typechecking, and main-project typechecking pass.
